core_question: Are the persons or objects being targeted lawful military objectives?
legal_function: Separates combatants/military objectives from civilians/civilian objects.
common_authorities: Additional Protocol I arts. 48, 51, 52; ICRC Customary IHL Rules 1 and 7
analysis_notes: Start every conduct-of-hostilities analysis with status and object classification.

core_question: Would expected incidental civilian harm be excessive in relation to the concrete and direct military advantage anticipated?
legal_function: Restrains attacks even when the target is military.
common_authorities: Additional Protocol I art. 51(5)(b); ICRC Customary IHL Rule 14
analysis_notes: Do not confuse jus ad bellum proportionality with IHL attack proportionality.

core_question: Were feasible precautions taken to verify targets and minimize civilian harm?
legal_function: Requires planning, verification, warnings where feasible, and choice of means and methods.
common_authorities: Additional Protocol I art. 57; ICRC Customary IHL Rules 15-21
analysis_notes: Evidence often turns on what was feasible based on information available at the time.

core_question: Is the measure directed toward a legitimate military purpose and not otherwise prohibited?
legal_function: Permits only measures necessary to accomplish a legitimate military aim within legal limits.
common_authorities: Hague Regulations; customary IHL; IHL commentaries
analysis_notes: Necessity never authorizes what IHL specifically prohibits.

core_question: Does the conduct avoid unnecessary suffering and protect persons hors de combat?
legal_function: Limits violence through humane treatment, medical protection, and bans on unnecessary suffering.
common_authorities: Common Article 3; Hague principles; Additional Protocol I; customary IHL
analysis_notes: Humanity operates across targeting, detention, medical care, and treatment of persons.
